review_note: Granted narrowly. Live native test test-beta-spatial-q2-sd-regression.R: 47 expectations, 0 failures, 0 skips on Totoro; the 3 manifest entries and the console-log hash match the current files. Oracle: a base-R dense Laplace (analytic score and Hessian, two starts of nlminb, finite-difference checks of score and Hessian) with a hand-built coordinate kernel K = exp(-distance/range) plus 1e-6 on the diagonal. K is built in the test from the raw 8x8 coordinates, and the test also compares the package's precision to solve(K) at 1e-10 and checks the range. The hand-built SD vectors exp(a + b*z) use z0 and z1 from the test. Both members are fitted (spatial intercept SD ~ z0 and spatial slope SD ~ z1, labelled coef selectors, independent fields). The oracle is compared with the logLik at 1e-4, and eta within 1e-4. My Totoro scratch run (R, taskset 166-167, pkgload at the worktree) reproduced the logLik difference of 8.9e-11 and gave these oracle gaps for emulated bugs: swapped z0/z1 selectors 100.8, reversed intercept SD 217.8, reversed slope SD 23.2, slope SD shifted 1 group 1.97, shifted 8 groups 11.8, kernel doubled 5.4, range doubled 4.9, kernel rows and columns shifted by 1 9.0 and by 8 20.0. All are at least 2e4 times the 1e-4 tolerance. Two perturbations are invisible by construction: cov2cor(K) (the diagonal is 1 + 1e-6, so the gap is 1e-11) and a reversal of kernel labels (the 8x8 grid kernel is point-symmetric, gap 0). The perturbations are from my scratch run, not asserted in the test. Does NOT establish: the optimiser optimum beyond the oracle comparison at the fitted parameters, recovery accuracy (the slope recovery is only within 0.4 on one seed), that cov2cor on the kernel is detected, a spatial range estimated rather than fixed, a mesh (SPDE) kernel, a correlated intercept-slope block, Julia parity, or interval coverage.
